diagnostic_evidence.quote: whose preimages $h^{-1}(s)$ we equip with the standard spherical measure $\sigma$ normalized so that $\sigma(h^{-1}(s))=1$.

issues.failure_explanation: For normalized surface measure on $S^d$, the first coordinate is not uniformly distributed on $[-1,1]$ except when $d=2$; its slice density is proportional to $(1-s^2)^{(d-2)/2}$. Thus the last equality is false for general $d$. For example, the displayed integral gives average $1/3$ to $f(\omega)=\omega_1^2$, whereas the spherical average is $1/(d+1)$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reparametrize the latitude coordinate according to the correct spherical slice density and verify that the resulting curve remains continuous, has the asserted length flexibility, and preserves pointwise use of the lower-dimensional design.
issues.overall_effect: The construction does not establish weighted designs on $S^d$ for $d>2$, invalidating the paper's all-dimensional weighted existence arguments.
issues.title: Uniform latitude integration is not spherical measure in general dimension
issues.why_classification: The conclusions may survive through a contained but nontrivial redesign of the latitude parametrization; the proof cannot be fixed by algebra alone.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds integrals of $f$ by length times $|\sup f|$, which is false when the negative minimum has larger magnitude than the maximum. More fundamentally, for normalized curves the literal definition forces exactness: for any polynomial $g$, apply it to $f=g-\sup g$, whose displayed right-hand side is zero, while the normalized functional annihilates constants. Thus the claimed approximate constructions are not established under Definition \ref{def:design}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $|\sup f|$ throughout by $\sup|f|=\|f\|_\infty$ and recheck every approximate-design estimate and claimed norm comparison under the corrected definition.
issues.overall_effect: The overlap estimate and all approximate-design existence results derived from it fail under the paper's literal definition.
issues.title: The approximate-design error uses absolute value of the maximum, not the supremum norm
issues.why_classification: The written definition collapses normalized approximate designs to exact designs, changing the central guarantee type; repairing it requires a global correction to the paper's principal notion and arguments.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: With notation as in the theorem statement, take $S$ to be the (finite) set of $s\in[0,1]$ such that $\gamma(s)$ is not smooth. Consider an open subset $\widetilde S\subset[0,1]$ such that $\ell(\gamma|_S)=\delta/2$
We may then smooth $\gamma$ to any curve $\widetilde\gamma$ which coincides with $\gamma$ on $[0,1]\setminus S$ and satisfies $\ell(\widetilde\gamma|_{S})=\delta/2$.

issues.failure_explanation: A finite parameter set $S$ has zero curve length, so it cannot satisfy $\ell(\gamma|_S)=\delta/2$ or support the proposed modification. In addition, $d\neq2$ includes $d=1$: every simple closed curve in $S^1$ has image the whole circle and length $2\pi$, so a simple curve of prescribed length $\ell(\gamma)+\delta$ need not exist.

failure_location.quote: If $d\neq2$, we may take $\widetilde\gamma$ to be simple.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use genuine open neighborhoods of the singular parameters and restrict the simplicity assertion to ambient dimension at least three, with a transversality or local detour argument controlling the added length and error.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed arbitrary-length smooth and simple perturbation is unsupported, including the dimension-one case relevant to the stated range of the paper.
issues.title: The smoothing lemma is false in dimension one and its construction uses zero-length finite sets
issues.why_classification: A contained smoothing argument can likely restore the higher-dimensional version, but the stated dimension-one scope must be weakened.
